ask.t: Padding should be opt-in, not default: add a .pad class you add where you need it (e.g. each tab's content area), rather than fighting off a default page padding.
On the Now card, chat stays a persistent right sidebar; the tiny top tabs should not include chat.
The Now card's tiny top tabs should be real routed pages using the page route mechanism, not hash identifiers.
The layout/padding skill should be invoked every time any layout is designed, possibly folded into the paging skill since paging already covers layout and navigation.
The dictation-to-chat pipeline is too slow: text took 4-5 seconds to appear after transcribing, and the assistant's response took about 5 more seconds; speed up both.

Selecting an element (e.g. a code block) through the hamburger/element picker shows a context pill but the assistant says it never sees that selected context when the message is sent; wire the selection through to the prompt.

Build a three-column layout explorer: left = layout categories (one/two-column, mobile vs mega), center = a large preview of the selected layout, right = sibling/child preview cards; clicking a right-rail card promotes it to center and its children become the new right rail, and every documented layout on the site gets its own page with a small flippable preview card.

Study and document the actual HTML nesting of sidebars/drawers/shells at every level of the site (home down to a framework page), and name the reusable sidebar slots (e.g. app.left / app.right) so a paging system can render into a named region and swap it, including whether nested or multiple sidebars are supported.
Make chat a reusable extension (ext/Chat) with a real streaming input/output system, so a reply is shown token by token as it's generated instead of only appearing once it's complete.

Give the fast and smart assistants each a chosen icon that doubles as their avatar and username inline next to each message (e.g. two arrows for Fast, a brain for Smart), instead of separate labeled blocks.

Add lightweight reactions to chat: the fast assistant can send a quick emoji (thumbs up, check mark) instead of a sentence when a simple acknowledgment is enough, falling back to one if the smart assistant hasn't replied in time.
When the owner references a specific thing in chat, keep it visible as a context card (the page's icon and name at the top, the related content inside) instead of only describing it in prose.
Build a standing, browsable catalog of the layout and navigation patterns actually used across every page on the site (not a one-off audit), so the systems can be browsed by usage.
Make sure tasks never get lost when many agents are working: every task/card should visibly nest under its parent card with a recognizable icon, so the owner can always see what belongs to what.

Fix the ask-by-voice sheet's header: it's misaligned with too much vertical space, drop the redundant back button (keep the X), make the header compact, and merge the settings gear and the overflow "more" button into one menu so the chat gets the remaining space.
Chat should auto-scroll to the newest message by default, stop doing so once the owner scrolls up, and show a "jump to bottom" button to return.
Add a "clean transcribe" mode toggle that sends dictation straight into the chat as it's spoken, with no separate editable text area, and consider making it the default.
Fix duplicate messages: assistant replies (and sometimes the owner's own transcriptions) are appearing twice in the same chat or card.
Restore the microphone start/stop sound cue; it stopped playing, so there's no audio signal that listening started or ended when not looking at the screen.
Replace the fixed-height audio level bar with a small pulsing dot that grows with volume, floats anywhere (e.g. bottom-right corner), and can be tapped to reopen the dictation sheet.

Build a text-to-speech "Voice" class/system, pairing with the existing Whisper dictation, with streaming output, switchable voices, and conversational timing rules (don't interrupt too soon) for a full voice-chat mode.
When a reply mentions a card or task, it must be a real clickable hyperlink, not plain text the owner has to copy and paste to navigate to.
Closing the dictation sheet should not stop the microphone from listening, and opening it can auto-start the mic — the two states (listening vs. sheet visible) should be independent.
Set up remote/mobile access to the site through a Cloudflare Tunnel (preferred over Tailscale or a new paid service, since Cloudflare is already in use) instead of relying on the local Wi-Fi IP.
Support threaded replies to one specific card or comment, not only appending to the general chat stream.
